title: Pen-test staging hardening & evidence onboarding checklist
content:
Purpose and intended use:
This is a working checklist and onboarding guide for an external penetration test run against Redwood Inference staging (non-prod) environment. Focus: ensure testers have scoped access, produce SIEM-ready evidence, document RBAC v2 considerations, and outline an initial remediation sprint plan. This doc is intentionally operational (checklists, TODOs, open questions).

Goals:
- Provide a deterministic evidence ingestion flow into our SIEM for pen-test artifacts
- Harden staging environment areas most likely to be exploited (webapp, API gateway, model serving endpoints, admin console)
- Minimize blast radius with temporary access policies for third-party testers
- Map findings to remediation owners and SLA-like timelines for staging fixes

High-level scope (what testers CAN target):
- Staging tenant: staging.redwood-inference.internal and associated subdomains
- API gateway endpoints (/**routes/**) in staging cluster only
- Admin console with staging credentials (provisioned test accounts)
- Dedicated model-serving nodes labeled staging-* (no VIPs to production hardware)
- CI artifact storage: staging-packages (read-only for testers)

Out-of-scope (explicit):
- Any production hostname, internal-only production networks, and real customer data stores
- External vendor integrations with production endpoints
- Hardware-level attacks on data center or cloud provider accounts

Pre-engagement checklist (before testers begin):
- ✅ Create a unique tester group in RBAC v2: role tester/external-<vendor>-<YYYYMM> (temporary TTL 14 days). Ticket: JIRA-SEC-412
- ✅ Create ephemeral SSH jumpbox accounts tied to tester OIDC (expires automatically)
- ✅ Provision test user accounts with MFA enforced (tester-1..N) for the admin console
- ✅ Generate an evidence-collection baseline: list of log streams and file drops that will be accepted by SIEM
- ✅ Snapshot staging infra (AMI/container images)/document versions for triage: image-tags, helm charts
- ✅ Notify SRE on-call window and provide Slack channel #sec-pt-<vendor>-<id>

Evidence ingestion & SIEM mapping (minimum deliverables):
- Required artifacts from testers:
  - HTTP request traces (start/end timestamps, full request/response headers if allowed, sanitized bodies)
  - Authentication attempt logs (user, method, source IP, timestamp)
  - SSH session recordings (ttyrec) for any jumpbox access
  - Proof-of-concept exploit artifacts (PoC code snippets, payloads, exploit replay instructions)
  - File system snapshots or relevant core dumps **only** when requested and authorized

- SIEM schema mapping (recommended fields):
  - event.time => ISO8601 timestamp (string)
  - event.source => hostname or service (e.g., api-gateway-01)
  - event.type => request | auth | shell | exploit | system
  - user.id => principal (service/user/test-account)
  - src.ip => source IP or connector id
  - http.method, http.path, http.status
  - rb.role => assigned RBAC role at time of event (rbac-v2 notation)
  - artifact.id => provided PoC filename or ticket id
  - evidence.tag => pen-test-vendor:<vendor>; test-id:<id>

- SIEM ingest specifics:
  - Preferred format: ndjson with one JSON event per line, UTF-8. If compressed, GZIP only.
  - S3 drop location: s3://redwood-pen-test-ingest/<vendor>/<test-id>/ (pre-provisioned) - provide presigned URL to testers.
  - If sending via syslog/HTTP collector, use the staging-collector with TLS and client certs (provide certs short-lived).

RBAC v2 considerations (staging):
- Use attribute-based constraints on tester role: allow list of actions rather than broad admin: e.g., allow: [read:api-logs, invoke:staging-models-limited], deny: [modify-deployments, change-rbac]
- Audit grant: every temporary role assignment must create an audit event with grant.reason and grant.grantor fields
- Session tagging: all sessions created for testers must include session.tag=pen-test/<vendor>/<id> so SIEM can filter and group

Evidence automation runbook (ops steps):
1) Pre-create S3 prefix and send presigned URL to vendor.
2) Ensure FluentD/Vector rule on staging is routing pen-test.* logs to dedicated SIEM index (pen-test-index).
3) Enable elevated retention for pen-test index (30d) and lock down write access to SOC team.
4) When tester uploads artifacts, the ingestion lambda should:
   - validate a signer token (from the temporary role)
   - normalize events to our schema (map fields listed above)
   - enrich events with geoip and known-internal-service flags
   - forward to SIEM with metadata: vendor/test-id

Open questions / TODO (actions owner):
- [ ] Decide default TTL for tester group (security proposed 14 days) - owner: Rafael Ortiz
- [ ] Confirm presigned S3 workflow with infra (Jenkins job vs API) - owner: Noah Patel
- [ ] Which PII sanitization rules are mandatory for PoC payloads? (legal + privacy input) - owner: Maya Singh

Triage and severity mapping (initial guidance):
- Critical: RCE or credential exfiltration of production-simulated secrets -> immediate containment and rollback on staging images; create hotfix; notify execs
- High: Broken auth allowing privilege escalation within staging RBAC -> 72h remediation SLA for staging; immediate temporary role revocation
- Medium: Info leak (internal endpoints returning internal hostnames or versions) -> 2 week remediation sprint
- Low: Footprinting noise, missing headers -> tracked in backlog

Remediation sprint plan (sample 2-week plan):
Week 0 (Triage & Containment):
- Day 0–1: SOC and infra freeze impacted staging artifacts. Short-term patches to disable vulnerable path.
- Day 2–3: Developers reproduce PoC in isolated sandbox and open PR with fix and test cases (link PR in ticket)
- Day 4: Hotfix deployed to staging with smoke tests; SOC validates by replaying PoC (if safe)

Week 1 (Root cause & longer-term fixes):
- Tasks: fix misconfigured RBAC policies, add unit/integration tests (auth flows), improve logging for missing fields
- Update: add audit log schema unit tests to infra/observability pipelines
- Deliverables: PRs merged, updated release notes, updated SIEM normalization for the specific findings

Acceptance criteria for remediation:
- Fix shipped to staging and verified by original PoC retainers or internal reproducer
- Audit events created for the offending action and visible in SIEM with rb.role and session.tag
- New test coverage preventing regression in CI: auth regression tests and log-schema tests

Communication & escalation matrix:
- Primary contact: Security engineer on call (sec-oncall@redwood.ai) and Slack #sec-pt-<vendor>-<id>
- Escalation 1: Security Lead - Rafael Ortiz (pager)
- Escalation 2: Head of Engineering - Maya Singh

Notes and heuristics (less formal):
- If a tester demonstrates a way to reach production-like config from staging (e.g., via misconfigured infra identity), treat as critical and assume wider impact until proven otherwise.
- Keep evidence chain-of-custody: upload PoC and associated logs to S3 with immutable tags; snapshot the tester session (ttyrec) for replay.
- Prefer reproducible test harnesses over raw memory dumps when possible (privacy + safety).

Appendix: sample minimal NDJSON event (one-line example)
{"event.time":"2024-11-05T14:23:12Z","event.source":"api-gateway-02","event.type":"request","user.id":"tester-external-acme-1","src.ip":"54.203.12.9","http.method":"POST","http.path":"/v1/models/generate","http.status":"500","rb.role":"tester/external-acme-202411","artifact.id":"poc-20241105-1.py","evidence.tag":"pen-test-vendor:acme;test-id:acme-20241105"}

References and artifacts to attach to the ticket:
- staging infra snapshot (AMI/container tags) - attach link when snapshot complete
- RBAC v2 role definition snippet (example policy JSON) - see CONFLUENCE-8482
- SIEM ingest lambda mapping code - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pulls/611

Last notes (operational hygiene):
- This doc will be iterated during the pre-engagement call with the vendor. Keep TODOs updated in the ticket.
- After engagement, produce a short "lessons learned" doc that includes false-positive signal noise, logging gaps, and recommended permanent infra changes.

-- Ava Chen (security engineer)
